subject: Recap: Acme Retail call — batching & pricing next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmeretail.com>, Todd Greene <todd.greene@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Acme Retail call — batching & pricing next steps

Hi Lena / Todd — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of call:
- Primary use case: catalog personalization + on-site search re-ranking (low latency snippets, ~1.2k TPS peak across inference cluster).
- Inference pattern: steady stream of user requests during daytime hours with short bursts for campaigns (expected 10–15% of baseline).
- Typical prompt/response size: avg 350 tokens in + 150 tokens out (total ~500 tokens per request).

Key asks we agreed to follow up on:
1) Volume confirmation: you mentioned 150M–300M tokens/month to start and potential 1–2B tokens in 12 months. Please confirm the baseline and peak monthly ranges.
2) Budget target: you gave a rough target of ~$18–$25k/month for model inference (target unit of measure: $/1M tokens). We want to map that to Redwood unit economics with batching.
3) Batching / concurrency assumptions: we discussed continuous batching expectations (steady-state batching vs spikes), target latency SLOs (~200–300ms P95), and concurrency limits per worker.

Deliverables from Redwood (attached):
- Redwood-Pricing-Estimate.pdf (initial per-1M token unit economics with 3 scenarios: baseline, optimized batching, and heavy-concurrency).
- SOW-draft.docx (high-level scope; we'll iterate once you confirm volumes).

Proposed next steps:
- Lena: confirm monthly token ranges (baseline and peak) and target budget band.
- Todd: confirm procurement timeline and whether a PO / SOW is required to start a pilot.
- Camila / Aditya: we will provide a refined estimate with explicit batching & concurrency assumptions and a recommended config for Dedicated vs Hosted if you need isolation.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk through the attached estimate and the continuous-batching assumptions.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

--
Attachments: Redwood-Pricing-Estimate.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmeretail.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Todd Greene <todd.greene@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Acme Retail call — batching & pricing next steps

Thanks Camila — good recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Volumes: baseline we expect ~200M tokens/month (current PoC traffic), with seasonal peaks pushing to ~350M for promotions. Our roadmap target is 1B tokens/month by EOY if performance and cost look good.
2) Budget: procurement has a budget envelope of $20k–$30k/month initially for inference (we can flex if the unit economics demonstrate clear cost savings). Our target unit is ~ $20 / 1M tokens but we understand effective $/1M will depend on batching and model choice.
3) Latency: P95 target for returned responses should be under 300ms for the search re-rank path. Re-ranking is the higher priority; personalization can tolerate slightly higher latency.

On batching: we expect continuous background traffic from users (steady-state) plus short bursts during email promotions. For steady-state, we have fairly uniform request distribution across a 12-hour peak window. For bursts, concurrency can spike 2–3x for ~10–15 minutes.

Procurement: Todd — can you confirm if Acme needs a signed SOW before we start a technical pilot or if a PO is sufficient?

Thanks,
Lena
Senior Product Manager — Personalization
Lena.Ortiz@acmeretail.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmeretail.com>, Todd Greene <todd.greene@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Acme Retail call — batching & pricing next steps

Lena — thanks for the clear numbers. Quick notes on how we model unit economics for $/1M tokens given continuous batching and concurrency patterns: 

1) Baseline assumptions we used in the attached estimate:
- Avg tokens/request: 500 (you confirmed ~500 total).
- Requests/day for 200M tokens/month ≈ (200M / 30) / (500/1) ≈ 13.3k requests/day (~9 requests/sec average over 24h, but concentrated during a 12h peak window -> roughly 18 RPS during peak).
- Continuous batching gains: with steady RPS (15–20 RPS) we expect the runtime to achieve effective micro-batching that increases GPU utilization ~2–3x versus naive single-request serving; this typically reduces effective $/1M tokens by ~30–45% depending on model and sequence lengths.
- Burst handling: for 2–3x short spikes, autoscaling + short-lived concurrency increases will handle spikes but unit economics during spikes will worsen (smaller effective batch sizes during the ramp). We size headroom for expected burst behavior.

2) Recommended configuration for pilot:
- Use a mid-size model variant Redwood-vanilla-13B quantized with continuous-batching enabled and 2x concurrency per worker. That hits a good balance of latency (P95 < 300ms) and unit cost.
- Autoscaling policy: scale on queue length + slow-start bursts; keep a small pool of warm workers to reduce cold-start latency.

3) Target pricing and negotiation guidance:
- If Acme can commit to a 6‑month reserved commit (Dedicated or committed capacity tier), we can price around $16–$20 / 1M tokens effective for the baseline volumes using aggressive batching assumptions and reserved capacity pricing.
- For a pure hosted, pay-as-you-go pilot at 200M tokens/month, expect $20–$28 / 1M depending on model variant and observed batching efficiency.

I'll attach a simple table of the scenarios to the estimate (Camila — included in the PDF). Happy to walk through numbers with Acme in a short call.

— Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmeretail.com>, Todd Greene <todd.greene@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Acme Retail call — batching & pricing next steps

Thanks Aditya & Lena. Action items and timeline: 

1) Acme (Lena): Confirm final baseline (we'll assume 200M/month) and confirm if you want to start on Hosted pilot vs Dedicated reserved pilot.
2) Acme (Todd): Confirm procurement path (PO vs SOW).
3) Redwood (Camila/Aditya): We will send an updated PDF estimate that includes the two scenarios Aditya called out (hosted pay-go vs 6-month reserved commit) and assumptions for continuous batching and expected effective $/1M tokens.

Proposed pilot plan: 1-month hosted pilot on our Hosted API with continuous-batching enabled, target 200M tokens/month cap, plus a short smoke test for promotional spikes (engineering team to run a synthetic 3x burst for 15 minutes). If pilot meets latency and cost targets, move to a 6-month committed capacity quote for preferred pricing.

I attached the updated Pricing Estimate and SOW draft. Please CC procurement and legal for the SOW comments.

Best,
Camila

From: Todd Greene <todd.greene@acmeretail.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Acme Retail call — batching & pricing next steps

Camila — procurement here. We can start with a PO for the pilot. If the pilot looks good, we'll need a signed SOW for the committed capacity term. I'll loop in Legal and Procurement; expect a PO to be issued within 1–2 weeks.

Todd Greene
